fallback.foundation: Foundation primitives have Build, Tools and Testkit reverse consumers, including installed and Wasm contracts.
fallback.build: Build changes require artifact, editor and optimizer owner qualification plus archive and private-driver contracts.
fallback.tools: Tools owns distinct external adapters and public identities; retain all isolated profiles and consumers.
fallback.testkit: Testkit owns simulator lifecycle, Wasm/probe singletons and installed/server contracts.

exclusions.reason: Focused tool admission retains host parsers, Cargo tools and the release editor. No selected contract installs the simulator or optimizer.
Focused lint, documentation and runtime tests retain the selected package and its admitted direct/reverse consumer contracts. Simulator-backed workspace tests have no edge to this scope.
Shared scripts, hooks, recipes and fixtures are unchanged from the complete three-host baseline; source/configuration changes select the full gate.
Foundation and Build implementations, dependencies and feature contracts are unchanged and have no production edge to Native or Text.
Native has no dependency or reverse consumer. Text retains its feature/graph checks, YAML profile and actual Tools icp-project consumer in the focused graph/test stages.
Public Testkit, simulator/server lifecycle and Wasm probe contracts do not consume Native or Text. The private driver’s Text rendering is exercised in focused tests.
Focused archive qualification uses the same IC Build archive engine, exact selected public package, normalized source/lock admission and installed archive tests.
Native has no Tools consumer. Text’s runtime caller is confined to icp-project, exercised separately; the remaining IC adapters do not use Text and are unchanged.
Wasm inspection does not depend on Native or Text; its source, graph and public identities are unchanged.
